requirements: Behance is free — 'no restrictions on the number of projects a member can create' and no upload limits (per Behance Helpcenter)
Projects must be original creative work — the community is for showcasing creative process, not generic link dumps
To publish: project needs content plus the required Settings fields — Cover Image, Project Title, and Creative Fields
Project must not be set to private to appear publicly
preparation: Project assets: images, videos, embedded media, or text arranged as a case-study-style project
Cover image, project title, creative field selection, and (recommended) tags and tools used
A SaaS launch fits only if framed as design/product work — e.g. UI case study, brand identity, product design process
workflow: Log in to your Behance profile
Click 'Share Your Work' at the top of the page and select Project
Add content via the Add Content panel (upload files, embed media, add text, or import from Lightroom); reorder as needed
Click Continue, then upload/select a Cover Image, enter a Project Title, select Creative Fields, and add Project Tags
Optionally set co-owners, credits, copyright/license, and adult-content flag
Click Publish (Save keeps it as a draft)
Promote the published project URL to social channels via the Promote option on the project
watchFor: Publish fails silently if required fields are missing — empty Content or missing Creative Fields blocks publishing
A project marked private never appears publicly — check Privacy Options if the project seems invisible
This is a portfolio community: a plain 'we launched a SaaS' post without design work reads as spam
Each project gets a unique URL plus View/Appreciation counters — those metrics are the traction signal
countsAsLive: The project is published (not a draft, not private) and reachable at its public behance.net/gallery/... URL with View/Appreciation counters
unknowns: Whether free accounts face any discoverability limits vs paid Adobe portfolio tools
Moderation/curation criteria for getting a project featured in a gallery
